symbols.name: transformed axes
symbols.meaning: The number of transformed axes, d-1.
symbols.quote: Write $\ell=\log_2 r$, the number of address bits of a long axis, and $D=d-1$, the number of transformed axes (not a chunk or a chunk count from the other pages).

symbols.name: leftover bits
symbols.meaning: The number of leftover low address bits of an axis after whole K-bit chunks are taken.
symbols.quote: Put $b=(\ell-1)\bmod K$, the number of leftover low bits of an axis, and $q=\lfloor(\ell-1)/K\rfloor$, its number of whole chunks.

symbols.name: whole chunks
symbols.meaning: The number of whole K-bit chunks of an axis.
symbols.quote: Put $b=(\ell-1)\bmod K$, the number of leftover low bits of an axis, and $q=\lfloor(\ell-1)/K\rfloor$, its number of whole chunks.

symbols.name: layout permutation
symbols.meaning: The record permutation defined by the prefix moves and chunk exchanges.
symbols.quote: The record permutation $L$, built below, moves them together once.

symbols.name: bit reversal
symbols.meaning: The bit-reversal permutation on all transformed axes.
symbols.quote: By [retained frequency order](frequency-order.md) the forward transform leaves its outputs in bit-reversed order, written $B$ here (the bit-reversal permutation on all axes), and the opposite transform consumes that order, so no reordering is executed.

symbols.name: interchange exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed exponent below 1 in the chunk-interchange cost.
symbols.quote: $K$ is the chunk width in bits, and $\tau,\lambda'<1$ are the interchange and layer exponents.

symbols.name: layer exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed exponent below 1 in the simultaneous-layer cost.
symbols.quote: $K$ is the chunk width in bits, and $\tau,\lambda'<1$ are the interchange and layer exponents.

relations.quote: The tape layout reorders the address bits of an array so that each round of a [synthetic polynomial transform](synthetic-transform.md) on several axes runs as one [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md) instead of one pass per axis, which is where the transform's cost drops below the standard pass count.

The tape layout reorders the address bits of an array so that each round of a [synthetic polynomial transform](synthetic-transform.md) on several axes runs as one [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md) instead of one pass per axis, which is where the transform's cost drops below the standard pass count.
This is at most $Dq-1$ exchanges, each done by the [fast address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md) in $O(TpK^\tau)$ even for nonadjacent chunks

By [retained frequency order](frequency-order.md) the forward transform leaves its outputs in bit-reversed order, written $B$ here (the bit-reversal permutation on all axes), and the opposite transform consumes that order, so no reordering is executed.

derivations.quote: Adding the three costs, the moves, exchanges and rounds give $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}])$.
